* Two deities are enshrined, both regarded as founder deities of cuisine and clan deities of the Takahashi no Omi:
:{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iwakamutsukari-no-Mikoto}} (イワカムツカリノミコト)
:{{ill|Takuhadachiji-hime|de|Yorozuhatahime|it|Takuhadachiji-hime|ja|栲幡千千姫命|ru|Ёродзухататоёакицуси-химэ-но микото|zh|栲幡千千姬命|qid=Q11110848}} (タチハタチヂヒメノミコト)

== History ==
The origin of Takahashi Shrine is unclear, but it appears certain that a place name "Takahashi" existed in this area in antiquity.

In the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ar|الإمبراطور سوجين|arz|الامبراطور سوجين|azb|سوجین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Sujin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوجین|cs|Sudžin|de|Sujin|el|Αυτοκράτορας Σουτζίν|es|Sujin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوجین|fr|Sujin|hr|Sujin|id|Kaisar Sujin|it|Sujin|ja|崇神天皇|ka|სუძინი|ko|스진 천황|ms|Maharaja Sujin|nl|Sujin|pl|Sujin|pt|Sujin|ru|Император Судзин|sh|Car Sujin|simple|Emperor Sujin|sl|Cesar Sudžin|sr|Суџин|sv|Sujin|th|จักรพรรดิซูจิง|tl|Emperador Sujin|tr|Sujin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Судзін|uz|Imperator Sujin|vi|Thiên hoàng Sujin|yo|Emperor Sujin|zh|崇神天皇|zh_classical|崇神天皇|zh_min_nan|Suzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|崇神天皇|qid=Q333530}}, an epidemic spread and many people died. The emperor, grieving, saw {{ill|Ōmononushi|fr|Ōmononushi|it|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主|mni|ꯑꯣꯃꯣꯅꯣꯅꯨꯁꯤ|ru|Омононуси|simple|Ōmononushi|zh|大物主|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi-no-Kami}} in a dream saying, "This epidemic is my will. If Ōtataneko worships me, the curse will disappear and the country will be at peace." The emperor then found Ōtataneko and had him worship Ōmononushi as priest, and the epidemic ceased as foretold. In this ritual, a person named Ikuto from Takahashi village in Soekami District, Yamato, was appointed as sake-offering attendant to present sacred sake.

Also, according to the entry for {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ar|الإمبراطور كيكو|arz|الامبراطور كيكو|azb|کیکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Keikō|cs|Keikó|de|Keikō|es|Keikō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کیکو|fr|Keikō (empereur)|hr|Keikō|hu|Keikó japán császár|id|Kaisar Keikō|it|Keikō|ja|景行天皇|ka|კეიკო|ko|게이코 천황|nds|Keikō|nl|Keiko (keizer)|no|Keiko (keiser)|pl|Keikō|pt|Imperador Keikō|ru|Император Кэйко|sh|Car Keikō|zh|景行天皇|zh_min_nan|Keikô Thian-hông|zh_yue|景行天皇|qid=Q329723}} year 53 in the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}},' when Keikō toured the east and reached {{ill|Kazusa Province|cs|Provincie Kazusa|de|Provinz Kazusa|es|Provincia de Kazusa|fa|ولایت کازوسا|fr|Province de Kazusa|gl|Provincia de Kazusa|hak|Kazusa-koet|id|Provinsi Kazusa|it|Kazusa|ja|上総国|ko|가즈사국|lt|Kadzusos žemė|nl|Kazusa (provincie)|pt|Província de Kazusa|ru|Кадзуса (провинция)|simple|Kazusa Province|sk|Kazusa (provincia)|sr|Провинција Казуса|tr|Kazusa (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кадзуса|zh|上總國|zh_classical|上總國|zh_min_nan|Kazusa-kok|zh_yue|上總國|qid=Q1055394}}, he obtained a white clam while crossing a sea route. The attendant deity prepared it as namasu and offered it, and the emperor greatly praised its taste, granting him the title of Kashiwade no Omi. Ten generations later, the title Takahashi no Ason was additionally granted. The ancestor of this Takahashi no Ason (Kashiwade no Omi) was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iwakamutsukari-no-Mikoto}}, and descendants hereditary-held Naizen duties for imperial meals; later they came to be worshiped as deity of cuisine. The change of surname from Kashiwade to Takahashi is thought related to this place name.

The former site was about 100 m north of the current location, but is said to have burned in warfare by {{ill|Matsunaga Hisahide|cs|Hisahide Macunaga|de|Matsunaga Hisahide|fa|ماتسوناگا هیساهیده|fr|Matsunaga Hisahide|it|Matsunaga Hisahide|ja|松永久秀|ko|마쓰나가 히사히데|ru|Мацунага Хисахидэ|sk|Hisahide Macunaga|sr|Мацунага Хисахиде|uk|Мацунаґа Хісахіде|zh|松永久秀|qid=Q1143038}} in the {{ill|Eiroku|ca|Eiroku|ckb|ئێیرۆکو|fa|ایروکو|fr|Ère Eiroku|ja|永禄|ko|에이로쿠|ru|Эйроку|simple|Eiroku|sr|Еироку|sv|Eiroku|tr|Eiroku|zh|永祿|qid=Q1143341}} era and moved to the present site. Later, three sacred mirrors were unearthed at the old site and are enshrined as shrine treasures.

== Rites ==
[[File:高橋神社 月次祭.jpg|150px|thumb|Takahashi Shrine monthly rite]]
== Hōtō-shiki ==
Every May, wishing prosperity of people bearing the Takahashi surname nationwide and advancement in culinary skills, the shrine performs "Hōtō-shiki," demonstrating the classical knife tradition {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōkusa-ryū Hōchōdō}}<ref name="産経ニュース">[https://www.sankei.com/article/20170515-SNG6BXYEIVOGBIHPANADTLZJRM/ "Hōtō-shiki" at Nara Takahashi Shrine; chief priest demonstrates elegant handling - Sankei News] viewed April 9, 2018</ref>. The rite existed from old times but had lapsed; from 2015 it was revived as a shrine ceremony<ref name="産経ニュース" />.
